extra.message: The 'p' query parameter (request.GET.get('p')) is joined with a static base path via os.path.join and opened directly with no sanitization. os.path.join discards the base path if 'filename' is absolute (e.g. p=/etc/passwd), and '../' sequences (e.g. p=../../../../badguys/settings.py) escape the images directory, allowing arbitrary file read from the server filesystem.

extra.message: User-supplied POST field 'first_name' is base64-decoded and passed directly to exec() (lines 72 and 76, Python 3 / Python 2 fallback paths). This allows an attacker to submit base64-encoded arbitrary Python code that is executed server-side with full application privileges (confirmed by the app itself checking for a resulting 'p0wned.txt' file).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: dor_user_profile() looks up and updates the in-memory 'users' dict purely by the 'userid' path parameter with no authentication or authorization check tying the requester to that user. Any client can POST to /direct-object-references/users/<id> and overwrite any other user's name/email (e.g. id=2, the admin account).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: missing_access_control() renders the admin-only template ('vulnerable/access_control/admin.html') solely based on the unauthenticated 'action' GET parameter equaling 'admin', with no session/role check. Any unauthenticated user can reach admin-only content by setting ?action=admin.

csrf_image() is decorated with @csrf_exempt, removing CSRF protection from this endpoint. Combined with the reflected XSS in the same view (qs parameter), a third-party site can force a victim's browser to trigger state-changing requests without a valid CSRF token.
django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out of MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, disabling Django's built-in CSRF protection for the entire application, not just the intentionally-exempt demo view.

unvalidated_redirect() passes the raw 'url' GET parameter straight to Django's redirect() with no allow-list or same-origin validation, letting an attacker craft a link on the trusted domain that redirects victims to an arbitrary external site (phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: unvalidated_forward() takes the 'fwd' GET parameter and uses it as a key into globals() to look up and invoke an arbitrary module-level callable with the current request object (function(request)). This lets an attacker invoke any function defined or imported in views.py (bypassing intended navigation/URL routing) purely by name.

extra.message: SECRET_KEY is a hardcoded, committed string rather than being loaded from an environment variable or secrets manager. Since SECRET_KEY underpins Django's session/cookie signing and CSRF tokens, a leaked/committed value lets an attacker forge signed sessions and CSRF tokens.

DEBUG = True is hardcoded (not environment-gated), and SHOW_TOOLBAR_CALLBACK (show_toolbar(), lines 180-185) enables the Django Debug Toolbar for any request carrying a 'debug' GET/POST param or cookie with no auth check. Together this lets any remote visitor trigger verbose stack traces (e.g. via /misconfiguration/boom) and interactive debug internals (SQL queries, settings, request data) on demand.
